strategies.summary: Replace the manual CUDA graph capture loop with torch.compile(fullgraph=True, backend='inductor') applied once in init_body. Inductor will fuse convolutions, batch norms, activations, and the skip-connection cats into fewer kernel launches and can exploit cudnn_benchmark internally, sidestepping the correctness issues seen with manual channels-last conversion.
implementation_hints: In init_body, after building all submodules, call self._compiled_forward = torch.compile(self._run_forward, fullgraph=True, backend='inductor', mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs') where _run_forward is a plain method that executes the full encoder-decoder chain.
In forward_stmt_1, dispatch to self._compiled_forward(x) when x.is_cuda and not self.training; fall back to the eager path otherwise.
Avoid passing self directly to torch.compile; extract the forward logic into a standalone function or use a module-level compiled wrapper to keep fullgraph=True viable.
Set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True in init_body to let cuDNN pick the fastest conv algorithm for the fixed spatial dimensions.
Do not apply channels-last conversion inside the compiled path; let Inductor handle layout decisions to avoid the correctness errors seen in n1/n4.
strategies.expected_gain: 10â25% wall-clock reduction from kernel fusion and elimination of Python dispatch overhead across 18+ sequential operations; Inductor often fuses BN+ReLU and conv+bias into single kernels.
risk_notes: fullgraph=True will fail if any graph break is introduced (e.g., data-dependent control flow); the compile call itself happens at first call, adding a one-time JIT cost.
max-autotune adds significant first-run latency; use 'reduce-overhead' mode if compilation time is a constraint.
Skip torch.compile on older CUDA/PyTorch versions where inductor support is incomplete.
forbidden_patterns: manual CUDAGraph inside the same path as torch.compile

review_notes.openai-compatible: Potentially strong upside from Inductor fusion and lower Python overhead, but `fullgraph=True` is brittle and compile/runtime support varies by PyTorch/CUDA stack. Useful if environment is modern and stable; otherwise medium execution risk.
review_notes.claude-compatible: torch.compile with max-autotune is the highest-leverage low-risk approach for a fixed-shape UNet. Inductor's BN+ReLU+conv fusion is well-documented and the fullgraph path avoids Python dispatch overhead across 18+ ops. Main risks are compilation latency and environment support, both manageable. Correctly avoids channels-last pitfalls from phase-1.
review_notes.gemini-compatible: Using torch.compile with fullgraph=True is the state-of-the-art approach for fusing operations and reducing overhead, often outperforming manual CUDA graphs with much less boilerplate.
